title: Nippon Life AMC Shares: Understanding the ₹9.50 Interim Dividend
description: Nippon Life India Asset Management has declared an interim dividend of ₹9.50 per equity share for its shareholders. The company has set October 28, 2026, as t.

faq.q: What is the difference between an interim and a final dividend?
faq.a: An interim dividend is declared and paid by a company during its financial year, usually based on its performance in a specific quarter or half-year. A final dividend, on the other hand, is declared after the company's full annual results are released and is approved by shareholders at the Annual General Meeting.

faq.q: Does the share price fall after the ex-dividend date?
faq.a: Generally, yes. On the ex-dividend date, the share price typically adjusts downwards by an amount roughly equivalent to the dividend per share. This is because new buyers on or after this date are not entitled to receive the declared dividend.

faq.q: How do I ensure I receive the dividend?
faq.a: To receive the dividend, you must purchase the shares before the ex-dividend date and ensure they are credited to your demat account by the record date. Your broker handles the settlement process, but buying a day or two before the ex-dividend date provides a buffer.

faq.q: Are dividends taxable for all investors in India?
faq.a: Yes, dividends received from Indian companies are taxable in the hands of the shareholder, irrespective of whether they are resident individuals or Non-Resident Indians (NRIs). TDS is also applicable above a certain threshold.

faq.q: Can NRIs claim a lower TDS rate on dividends?
faq.a: NRIs may be able to claim a lower TDS rate on dividends if their country of residence has a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) with India that specifies a lower rate. They would need to provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and Form 10F to the company or its registrar.
